tier_reason: The benchmark code is public (feldroop/rust-fmindex-benchmark src/main.rs, src/common_interface.rs, justfile), the CPU is stated (Xeon Gold 6348) and the flags are stated (cargo --release, -C target-cpu=native in .cargo/config.toml), but the rustc version is not stated anywhere (no rust-toolchain file; edition 2024 only implies rustc >= 1.85), so it misses A; the benchmark was run by the genedex author, so it is first-party C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc, version not stated (no rust-toolchain file; Cargo.toml edition 2024 implies rustc >= 1.85); cargo run --release (profile.release with debug = true) with RUSTFLAGS -C target-cpu=native from .cargo/config.toml; dependency versions pinned in Cargo.lock (genedex 0.2.2, bio 3.0.0)
corrections.caveats: Benchmark author is the genedex author (bias alert stated in the benchmark README). Baselines are other Rust crates (rust-bio, fm-index, sview-fmindex); no run against SDSL (C++) or sux. rustc version not stated. Numbers come from the Locate-Hg38.svg plot; the same values are embedded as text labels in the SVG source. Index construction for genedex used 8 threads (-t 8) while the search loop is single-threaded and best of 5. AWRY was excluded from this benchmark for segmentation-fault problems. Only DNA/hg38 workload. An independent benchmark (RagnarGrootKoerkamp/quadrank evals/fm.csv, i7-10750H) uses genedex as a baseline: genedex flat64 sequential count of simulated 150 bp reads took 4.18 s on 1 thread versus AWRY 8.56 s, while QuadFm prefetch took 1.31 s, so genedex is not the fastest Rust FM-index there.

notes: All seven Locate-Hg38 running-time and memory values in claimed_speedup match the text labels inside Locate-Hg38.svg (bio large 7.0 s/19.9 GB, bio small 10.2/10.2, fmindex multi text 87.9/7.3, cond64 2.6/5.2, flat64 1.6/7.2, sview vec128 2.4/5.4, vec32 2.3/6.9). Harness and CPU are stated but rustc version is not, per the orchestrator's A condition; note the quadrank precedent kept A with only a minimum rustc stated, so the orchestrator may choose to restore A for consistency.

The one third-party measurement found (quadrank evals/fm.csv) shows AWRY slower than genedex, so there are no numbers showing AWRY faster than a named baseline.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 5 stars on UM-Applied-Algorithms-Lab/AWRY (283 commits, 6 forks); 0 on the traviswheelerlab fork; on crates.io (awry 0.3 used by rust-fmindex-benchmark)
corrections.caveats: traviswheelerlab/AWRY is a fork of UM-Applied-Algorithms-Lab/AWRY (BSD-3-Clause, last commit 2025-01-14), which is the upstream. No AWRY benchmark in either README; the 'fastest in its class' claim and the 2-4x (nucleotide) / 2-6x (amino acid) speedups over SeqAn3 belong to the C library AvxWindowFmIndex (doi 10.1186/s13015-021-00204-6, snippet only, not opened). feldroop/rust-fmindex-benchmark excluded AWRY for segmentation faults and reports 18x peak construction memory. Third-party numbers in RagnarGrootKoerkamp/quadrank evals/fm.csv (i7-10750H, simulated 150 bp reads on a human genome, built from a patched fork) show AWRY slower than the alternatives: sequential count 8.56 s on 1 thread versus genedex flat64 4.18 s (about 2.0x slower, derived from page data), and 872 s index build versus about 109 s for genedex.

notes: Kept at tier D per the seed-record rule; repo_url corrected to the upstream as instructed. The only measurement found shows AWRY losing to genedex, so it has no demonstrated speed win; the orchestrator may prefer to file it as a documented non-winner.
